name: Ketorolac
executiveSummary: NSAID analgesic for short-course moderate–severe acute pain. Adult IV/IM 30 mg every 6–8 h (max 120 mg/day); pediatrics 0.5 mg/kg IV or 1 mg/kg PO per dose with strict ceilings. Treatment ≤ 48–72 h.
indications:
## Indications

- Short-course moderate to severe acute pain (postoperative, colic, trauma) when potent non-opioid analgesia is needed or as adjunct.
- Oral continuation after parenteral start in adults/adolescents per label.

## Precautions and contraindications

- Contraindicated in moderate–severe renal failure, active peptic ulcer/GI bleeding, high bleeding risk, pregnancy/labor, NSAID hypersensitivity.
- **Usual maximum duration: 48–72 h** (combined parenteral + oral).
- Halve dose in mild renal impairment (max 60 mg/day IV) and in ≥ 65 years per label.

> Does not replace opioids in all settings; assess renal function and GI risk before each dose.

adulto.presentation: Ampoules 15 mg/mL or 30 mg/mL; tablets 10 mg.
adulto.dose: ≥ 17 years and ≥ 50 kg: IV/IM **30 mg every 6–8 h**; max **120 mg/day**. If < 50 kg or ≥ 65 years: **15 mg every 6–8 h**; max **60 mg/day**. PO (continuation): **10 mg every 6–8 h**; max **40 mg/day**. Common single IV loading dose: 30 mg (15 mg if < 50 kg/elderly).
adulto.administration: IV: slow push > 15 s or intermittent infusion diluted (~0.12 mg/mL) in 0.9% NaCl or 5% dextrose over 1–5 min. Deep IM. PO with or without food.
adulto.notes: Precipitates with morphine in the same line. Dialysis removes little drug. Do not combine with other NSAIDs.

pediatrico.dose: 6 months–16 years: IV **0.5 mg/kg/dose** (max **15 mg/dose**) every 6–8 h. PO: **1 mg/kg/dose** every 6–8 h (max **10 mg/dose**). If < 50 kg: IV daily ceiling **60 mg/day**. ≥ 17 years / ≥ 50 kg: see adult.
pediatrico.administration: Slow or diluted IV. PO with syringe/tablet per presentation.
pediatrico.notes: Maximum duration 48–72 h. Contraindicated in moderate–severe renal failure. Mild renal impairment: half dose, max 60 mg/day IV, with renal monitoring.

neonatal.dose: Do not use under 6 months unless exceptional referral-center protocol.
neonatal.notes: Immature renal function: high risk of AKI and bleeding.

stability:
## Stability / storage

- Ampoule: use after opening; discard remainder.
- Intermittent infusion dilution: prepare extemporaneously per label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, dyspepsia, epigastric pain, constipation/diarrhea, edema, hypertension, rash, pruritus, somnolence, dizziness, headache, sweating. Serious: GI bleeding, thrombocytopenia, seizures, AKI.
